chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about one who reads in the muṣḥaf while he is without wudu (ablution). He said: “There is no harm, but he should not touch the Book.”

key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: the Book, here referring to the written Qur'an
key_terms.الْمُصْحَفِ: the written codex of the Qur'an
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: ritual ablution required for states of taharah (ritual purity)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to read the Qur'an from the muṣḥaf without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning reciting from the muṣḥaf without wudu (ablution). It indicates that reading is permitted in that state, while touching the written Qur'an itself is not allowed.
